spectrum.absolute_power_definition: One-sided |FFT(w*residual)|^2/(Nfft*sum(w^2)); sum equals Hann-weighted residual mean square; DC excluded from reported total.
spectrum.amplitude_definition: 2*|FFT|/sum(Hann); coherent single-sinusoid amplitude estimate, not a confidence bound.
spectrum.review_method: Retain every resolution-separated actual maximum, without a maximum-relative power cutoff or a fixed peak count. Review local prominence and absolute strain amplitude, then require consistent peak frequency/amplitude under a Blackman-window comparison to flag Hann leakage, and actual atom rebinning with a half-x-bin origin shift and neighboring Gaussian smoothing widths. Same-grain far-field signed strain uses the same x window, binning, baseline, z channel and physical power units. Shared far-field peaks are descriptive evidence and never a veto: elastic fields may extend into the far field. These are fixed review heuristics, not significance tests.

review_policy.window_sensitivity_check: Hann versus Blackman; matched actual peak coherent amplitude ratio must be in [0.5, 2] and exceed the absolute floor

absolute_spectrum.absolute_power_definition: One-sided |FFT(w*residual)|^2/(Nfft*sum(w^2)); sum equals Hann-weighted residual mean square; DC excluded from reported total.
absolute_spectrum.amplitude_definition: 2*|FFT|/sum(Hann); coherent single-sinusoid amplitude estimate, not a confidence bound.
absolute_spectrum.review_method: Retain every resolution-separated actual maximum, without a maximum-relative power cutoff or a fixed peak count. Review local prominence and absolute strain amplitude, then require consistent peak frequency/amplitude under a Blackman-window comparison to flag Hann leakage, and actual atom rebinning with a half-x-bin origin shift and neighboring Gaussian smoothing widths. structure_fft.method: Count atoms in separate y/z density channels; remove each channel's linear x trend, apply a Hann window, and sum squared x-FFT magnitudes. Do not sum complex amplitudes or project atoms onto x before the transform. This is a pure-x spectral-power marginal, not a full xyz translation validation.
structure_fft.peak_review_method: Retain actual local maxima separated by 0.75 native frequency bins without a global-relative-power threshold. Review uses local prominence, agreement under a half-bin transverse-origin shift, and spectral-shape contrast against each available far-field grain on the same x window/grid. Normalize each spectrum by its total positive-frequency power; this compares power fractions, not absolute scattering intensity, and no spectrum is subtracted. Background is the largest reference power fraction within half a native bin, regularized by max(reference median power fraction, 1e-6 of its largest fraction). These are review heuristics, not statistical significance or evidence of a dislocation.

peak_review_policy.interpretation: Fixed review heuristics, not a detection probability; every resolution-separated local maximum remains in local_peaks regardless of review eligibility.

interpretation_limits: Layer-resolved power prevents phase cancellation but discards relative phases; shared spectral peaks do not establish a full xyz translation.
No x/y periodic wrapping or artificial atom replication is used; z positions wrap into the original physical cell.
Band power is grid- and selection-dependent; a separately normalized long-band peak can carry little total power.
Harmonics, finite-window leakage and density-bin boundary sensitivity remain possible; peak resolution ranges are not confidence intervals.
The legacy peaks list retains the former 5%-of-band-maximum display rule for compatibility; local_peaks and review_peaks do not use that global gate.
Far-field comparison measures spectral-shape redistribution, not absolute density/scattering amplification; disorder can change its positive-frequency normalization denominator.
No wavelength multiple or harmonic is deleted; a strong bulk-reference peak overlap is a flag, not a veto on structural evidence.
A lattice peak shifted by local homogeneous strain beyond the half-native-bin background tolerance may appear enhanced; enhancement does not certify a non-lattice origin.
structure_fft.reference_selection_policy: Complete contiguous far-field bands validated by PTM purity, with the same x window and free-edge exclusions. No RMSD-quantile thinning: masks used for lattice-constant fitting are intentionally not reused.

Review uses local prominence, agreement under a half-bin transverse-origin shift, and spectral-shape contrast against each available far-field grain on the same x window/grid. Normalize each spectrum by its total positive-frequency power; this compares power fractions, not absolute scattering intensity, and no spectrum is subtracted. Background is the largest reference power fraction within half a native bin, regularized by max(reference median power fraction, 1e-6 of its largest fraction). These are review heuristics, not statistical significance or evidence of a dislocation.
structure_fft_review.meaning: Background-aware review is heuristic evidence, not a statistical significance test or an identified dislocation period.

long_band_policy.meaning: Exploratory zoom interval, not a proven division between short motifs and dislocation scales. Summary uses the same absolute strain power for full and long bands; independently band-normalized arrays remain supplemental only.

interpretation_limits: All audited actual maxima remain in strain_fft_peaks.csv and the profile local_peaks arrays; review eligibility is a heuristic, not statistical significance.
No expected orientation ratio or dislocation spacing enters this calculation.
Far-field a is an effective reference and includes pre-existing homogeneous strain; a scalar cannot remove anisotropy.
PTM and elastic strain share atomic coordinates and are not independent statistical measurements.
No strain signal is not evidence that a coordinate period or a dislocation is absent.
Signed strain is primary: mixing grains can cancel opposite signs; absolute/squared strain can introduce half-periods.
The two z half-channels test transverse consistency, not a full 3D elastic-field translation proof.
Spectral resolution ranges are not confidence intervals; finite window, free surfaces and smoothing can shift peaks.
Local extrema intervals, FFT wavelengths and whole-pattern recurrence are distinct observations; none automatically establishes a dislocation identity.
Summary strain panels use common absolute strain-squared power units, including far-field curves; separately normalized relative_power arrays are supplemental shape evidence only.
Same-grain far-field overlap is descriptive and never a rejection condition; a real elastic field may extend into the far field.

multiscale_review.meaning: Primary summary combines structure/strain spectra, spatial features and every coordinate candidate with direction ratios; a display highlight is review priority, not a selected physical period.
